subject: Clarify: default log persistence (requests, prompts, outputs)

Subject: Quick Q on default log retention and residency

Hi Marissa,

Hope youre well. As we get closer to the procurement review, legal has a couple of targeted questions about Redwood's hosted default retention settings for API traffic. Specifically: 

- For hosted API customers, what is the default retention window for full request/response logs (including prompts and model outputs)?
- Are prompts/outputs stored differently from telemetry (latency/metrics)?
- Is the data stored in-region by default (our data policy prefers US-only storage)?

Can you confirm what customers see out-of-the-box and what options exist to shorten retention or opt-out (without Private deployment)? Were documenting a list of must-haves for the contract.

Thanks,
Robert Hayes
Security Lead, Acme Financial

Robert,

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: for Redwood Hosted the default retention for request/response content (prompts + outputs) is 30 days; telemetry and aggregated metrics are retained separately. We can provide more formal language for contract exhibits.

I'm looping in Vivek (ops) and Neha (security) to give precise wording and options for tighter retention or in-region guarantees. 

Quick clarifications while were aligning:
- The 30-day window is the default for request/response content; customers can request shorter retention for hosted accounts (we have a 0/7/30 policy options page and an enterprise addendum to lock it).
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) leave all logs under customer control.
- We'll confirm residency details below.

I'll follow up with a short PDF summary for legal.

Subject: Re: Quick Q on default log retention and residency

Robert — adding a couple operational notes so legal sees the engineering controls: 

- Default retention: 30 days for full request/response payloads on hosted plans. This includes prompt text and model outputs stored in object stores tied to the customer's region where available.
- Telemetry/metrics: aggregated metrics (latency, token counts, error rates) are retained for 365 days for platform health and billing reconciliation; these are pseudonymized and stored separately from PII.
- Shortening retention: Hosted customers can request contract-level retention changes; for standard self-serve accounts theres a retention toggle (30 -> 7 -> 0) we can apply during onboarding for qualified customers — some changes require an enterprise addendum.
- Deletion semantics: deletion requests are processed asynchronously; deleted request/response records are expunged from live storage and queued for background erasure from backups (up to 90 days for immutable backup retention, documented in the addendum).

I'll let Neha provide the compliance/legal phrasing.

-- Vivek
VP, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick Q on default log retention and residency — detailed Q&A

Hi Robert — following up with a security/compliance-focused breakdown that you can paste into your questionnaire. Ive kept the answers concise and contract-friendly. Happy to jump on a short call if legal wants exact exhibit language.

1) Default retention windows (hosted):
- Request/Response payloads (prompts, raw model outputs): 30 days by default.
- System/Telemetry metrics (latency, errors, aggregated token usage): 365 days (pseudonymized).
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: retained per-customer settings; default is 30 days but may be extended if explicitly enabled by the customer.

2) Residency: 
- Data is stored in the region associated with the customer's primary account region (US/EU/APAC) when that region is available. For US-only storage requests, we can provide a written commitment in the enterprise addendum and route all eligible storage and processing to US regions.

3) Deletion and erasure: 
- Customer-initiated deletion: we expose an API and console workflow to purge request/response logs. After initiation we mark records for immediate inaccessibility; background erasure from backups can take up to 90 days.
- Compliance deletions (e.g., GDPR data subject requests): we support scoped exports and erasures and will coordinate timelines in the Data Processing Addendum (DPA).

4) Opt-out / minimal retention options: 
- Self-serve customers: retention toggle (30/7/0) available during onboarding; setting to 0 means prompts/outputs are not persisted beyond ephemeral processing buffers.
- Hosted customers requiring 0 retention as an SLA term: available via enterprise contract (we will require an attestation of allowed functionality tradeoffs).

5) Auditability and attestations:
- We publish SOC 2 Type II reports and can provide an audit artifact for retention configuration upon request.

Attachments: Redwood-Hosted-Retention-Summary.pdf (short explainer)

If you need sample DPA language, I can paste a clause; otherwise I can send the standard addendum that lists backup retention windows and deletion SLA.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
